eval.question: What is the Tokenomics Foundation's published formula for Cache Hit Rate, and what is the publication status of the page it comes from?
eval.expected: Cache hit rate = cache read / (cache read + cache write + uncached input). Source: the Prompt Cache Explainer, Release Candidate 1 (2026-09-22).

eval.question: A workload last week had 800,000 cache-read tokens, 50,000 cache-write tokens and 150,000 uncached input tokens. Base input price is $3 per million tokens, cache reads bill at 0.1x and cache writes at 1.25x. What are its Cache Hit Rate and Cache Cost Efficiency?
eval.expected: Cache hit rate 0.8 (80%). Uncached equivalent cost $3.00, actual prompt cost $0.8775, Cache Cost Efficiency 0.7075 (about 70.8%) — clearly above zero, so caching is paying for itself.

eval.question: In Big-T notation, what do the three variables in T(n · k · a) stand for, and what is the published fix for the agent-multiplicative class?
eval.expected: n = requests, or input size; k = model calls per request; a = agent depth. Fix for T(n·k·a): "Bound agent depth; add circuit breakers and budgets."

eval.question: Which layers of the Five-Layer Tokenomics Stack move the Big-T multiplier, and what is the key metric for the inference stack layer?
eval.expected: L3 Inference stack, L4 Model management and selection (model and quantization), and L5 Routing and governance move it; L1 Silicon and L2 Capacity do not (they set cost per token / effective cost per token). L3's key metric: cache hit rate, time to first token, throughput.

eval.question: What token reductions does the Big-T explainer publish for code-generation mode and for filtered retrieval, and which Big-T class does each land in?
eval.expected: Code-generation mode: ~80%, T(n). Filtered retrieval (RAG done right): 92–99.9%, T(log n). (Standard tool calls are the baseline at T(n·k).)

eval.question: According to the cache explainer's provider snapshot, which provider charges nothing for cache writes, and what minimum cacheable prefix does Anthropic document? When were the provider docs reviewed?
eval.expected: Google (Gemini API) has no write charge (implicit caching only). Anthropic: model-dependent, 512 to 4,096 tokens. Provider docs reviewed Aug 2026.

eval.question: Which FOCUS 1.5 work item adds the TokenCacheAction property, what values can it carry, and what is its status on the Foundation's tracker?
eval.expected: FR 2099 (the cached-token work), in review (Member review). TokenCacheAction carries "Uncached", "Read", "Write", or "Other"; it ships with TokenDirection ("Input"/"Output") and replaces the drafted TokenType. It is not in a ratified FOCUS release.

eval.question: Which FinOps Framework capabilities does the Tokenomics Foundation's material itself link to the FinOps Practitioner persona, and what finops:// URIs identify them?
eval.expected: Anomaly Management, Allocation, Budgeting, Forecasting — finops://framework/capabilities/anomaly-management, /allocation, /budgeting, /forecasting — each with an evidence quote from the Personas and Operating Model page (Release Candidate 2).

eval.question: Which value classification outcome categories belong to the labor group, and to which five destinations does Finance book realized value?
eval.expected: Labor: capacity gain, labor augmentation, labor automation. Booking destinations: new revenue won, revenue retained, spend removed, spend avoided, capital freed.

eval.question: How does the Tokenomics Foundation define "tokenmaxing", and is the definition page a ratified standard?
eval.expected: "The now-cautionary habit of running everything through the most powerful model because tokens felt free." Source: "What is AI Tokenomics?" — a Working Draft (June 2026), not a ratified standard.
